# Ontario Apartment Rental Basics

You likely have a standard Ontario residential tenancy, so the key issues are: **deposit rules**, **habitability/repair duties**, and **how to document problems early**. Your move-in heater issue is especially important because landlords must keep rental units in a good state of repair.

## Tenant Rights, Documentation Checklist, and Deposit Clarification

| Topic | What it means in Ontario | What you should do now |
|---|---|---|
| Lease term | A 12-month lease is binding for the fixed term you signed. | Keep a copy of the signed lease and note the start date: **2026-02-01**. |
| Security deposit | Ontario generally does **not** allow a “damage deposit” for normal wear/tear. Deposits are usually limited to things like **last month’s rent** and a **key deposit** if reasonable. | Ask the landlord, in writing, what the deposit was for and request a receipt/itemization. |
| Broken heater at move-in | The landlord is generally responsible for maintaining the unit, including heat if it is part of the rental and required by law/lease. | Report the issue immediately in writing and ask for a repair timeline. |
| Move-in condition | Pre-existing defects matter for responsibility and later disputes. | Take dated photos/video and write a move-in condition list. |
| Repairs | Keep records of all repair requests and replies. | Save emails/texts, and follow up if there’s no response. |
| Escalation | If the landlord does not fix the issue, Ontario has formal tenant remedies. | Keep your evidence organized for the Landlord and Tenant Board if needed. |

### What to document right away
- Signed lease and any addenda
- Proof of all payments: deposit, first month’s rent, receipts, bank transfer records
- Photos/video of the broken heater and any other defects
- Date/time you moved in and when you first noticed the issue
- All messages with the landlord or property manager
- Any temperature readings or notes showing the apartment is unheated or unsafe
- Names of witnesses, if anyone saw the condition at move-in

### Tenant-rights checklist for your situation
- Confirm whether the deposit was actually **last month’s rent** or something else
- Ask for a written explanation if the landlord called it a **damage deposit**
- Request repair of the heater immediately
- Keep communication polite, factual, and in writing
- Do not withhold rent without getting advice first
- Save everything in one folder with dates

## Polite Repair and Deposit Message Template

Hi [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I’m writing about two items from move-in on **2026-02-01**.

First, the heater in the apartment was not working when I moved in. Please let me know when this can be inspected and repaired, since heat is needed for the unit to be livable and comfortable.

Second, I paid a deposit that was described as a “damage deposit.” Could you please confirm in writing what this deposit is for and provide a receipt or breakdown of how it will be handled?

For my records, I would appreciate a written response with the repair timeline and deposit clarification.

Thank you,
[Your Name]
[Unit Address]
[Phone or Email]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Ontario Tenant Rights](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
Action: [Button: Landlord and Tenant Board](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)

## Sources

- Ontario tenant rights: https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights
- Landlord and Tenant Board: https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/
- Residential Tenancies Act overview: https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17
